_meta.description: Tier A physiological and Tier B aging/healthspan outcomes.
higher_is_policy: higher_is encodes ONLY whether a higher measured value is unambiguously better or worse for the organism, independent of context, genotype, diet, ambient temperature and time of day.

For almost every Tier A physiological variable this is NOT the case: higher food intake, energy expenditure, sympathetic activity, core temperature, heart rate or corticosterone is adaptive in some contexts and pathological in others. Those entries are null.
null is the expected value. It is set deliberately, not because the field was unfilled.
This field must never be aggregated into a composite score. SCHEMA.md section 6 forbids a rejuvenation score, and summing higher_is across outcomes would be exactly that.
polarity_policy: Two hazards, both the subject of DECISIONS.md D-019, which this vocabulary cannot resolve on its own because the fix is a reading judgement.

inverted_synonyms: the quantity these words name moves OPPOSITE to the quantity this entry is named for. Insulin resistance rising is insulin sensitivity falling. Longer sleep latency is less sleep. A record whose outcome_raw matches one of these must have had its direction inverted to describe THIS entry's quantity, and extraction_notes must say so.

signed_synonyms: these words already carry a direction or name a clinical state. direction must describe the CHANGE in this entry's quantity, never the presence of the state. 'Reduced hyperglycemia' is blood_glucose decrease, not increase.
A synonym matching the words in a paper does not make this the right outcome_id. Where the vocabulary holds the literally measured quantity, that entry wins (D-019 step 1).
These lists are not exhaustive and are not a substitute for reading. They record the traps found so far, and must never be used to rewrite a direction automatically.
changelog: 0.2.0: renamed `cognitive_decline` to `cognitive_performance` and moved its two signed synonyms to inverted_synonyms, adding `escape latency`. The old id named a quantity and its negation at once, which made `direction` ambiguous before a curator even read the paper. No curated record used the id, so the rename costs nothing. See docs/DECISIONS.md D-029.

0.3.0: annotated 4 genuinely inverted synonyms -- `fat oxidation` and `lipid oxidation` under `rer`, `wakefulness` and `arousal` under `sleep` -- and moved `insomnia` and `sleep fragmentation` to `signed_synonyms` where they belong. Found when a curator hit the RER / fat oxidation trap in doi:10.1038/s41467-018-08239-x. Annotation only: no code reads these lists, no id changed, and no stored direction was rewritten. See docs/DECISIONS.md D-049.

0.4.0: stated what a Tier A outcome IS (scope_policy) and what it is not (out_of_scope_readouts), and removed `EEG delta power` from `sleep`. Prompted by a reader asking whether EEG helps when it records the cortex rather than the hypothalamus -- a boundary the project had never written down, stated only as one clause of D-054. The rule is state-of-the-organism versus activity-of-neurons, not central versus peripheral, because `inflammatory_markers_other` deliberately admits central glial markers as a declared proxy for systemic inflammation and a central/peripheral rule would have retroactively invalidated it. One deletion, no id changed, no stored direction rewritten. See docs/DECISIONS.md D-063.

0.5.0: split `sleep` into the five vigilance-state quantities it had been pooling -- `nrem_sleep`, `rem_sleep`, `wakefulness`, `sleep_latency`, `sleep_fragmentation` -- and re-scoped `sleep` to the composite readout that does not resolve to one state. NREM and REM are not complements and move independently, so one id for both manufactured contradictions in the claim key, the same defect class as D-050 and D-052. `wakefulness` and `sleep latency` stop being inverted synonyms and become their own quantities, which removes a hand-flip from the curator. Bare `arousal` is deliberately a synonym of nothing: it names the waking state in one literature and a count of awakenings in the other. Prerequisite for curating the 334 admissible state-amount units in the EEG seam. See docs/DECISIONS.md D-064.

0.5.1: added the elided forms `NREM` and `non-REM` to `nrem_sleep` and `REM` to `rem_sleep`. The matcher is a word-boundary alternation over synonyms, so "NREM and REM sleep both decreased" matched only `rem_sleep` (47 units) and "REM and NREM sleep" matched only `nrem_sleep` (12 units) -- each ordering silently lost its elided half. Bare `REM` also fires inside `non-REM sleep`; measured at 25 units, all of which discuss REM in their own right, so it never fires alone here. Accepted deliberately: a proposer's false candidate is reviewable, a missed one is not. See docs/DECISIONS.md D-070.

0.5.2: moved `cataplexy` and `narcolepsy` into sleep.signed_synonyms. Both were carried into sleep.synonyms by the D-064 split and never checked against the polarity policy that `insomnia` -- the third clinical-state word in the same list -- already satisfied, so two of the three traps sat unmarked. A batch-2 reader walked into one. D-087.
scope_policy: A Tier A outcome is a STATE OF THE ORGANISM, or a tissue measurement the literature uses as a declared proxy for one. It is not the ACTIVITY OF NEURONS (D-063).

SCHEMA.md 1 makes the unit (population) x (perturbation) x (physiological readout). Neural activity sits on the perturbation side of that product: it is how a manipulation is verified to have worked, not what the manipulation did to the animal. Recording it as an outcome would put the same quantity on both sides of the record.

The instrument is not the test. `sleep` is measured with EEG/EMG and is in scope, because what it reports is minutes per hour of a whole-animal state; the electrodes are no more the readout than a calorimeter is.

A central measurement CAN be in scope when the field reports it as the systemic readout, and `inflammatory_markers_other` is the standing example: it admits microglial activation, Iba1, GFAP and gliosis, and its notes say why. The requirement is that the proxy be stated, not that the tissue be peripheral.

out_of_scope_readouts lists what this rule excludes. The list is not exhaustive and is not a licence: a readout absent from it is not thereby in scope. Extending the vocabulary is a decision entry, never a curator's judgement mid-pass (D-054).

out_of_scope_readouts._note: neural_activity is excluded by the scope policy above. behavioural_affective was already excluded by D-054, which declined these readouts during the circuit pass because Tier A is systemic physiology; listing them here makes that refusal checkable instead of remembered.

blood_glucose.label: Blood glucose concentration
blood_glucose.notes: Direction of benefit depends entirely on the baseline state (hypoglycemia vs diabetic hyperglycemia).

glucose_tolerance.label: Glucose tolerance (GTT)
glucose_tolerance.notes: Reported either as glucose AUC (higher = worse tolerance) or as 'tolerance' (higher = better). The sign of the reported quantity is assay-dependent, so no global valence. POLARITY: raw glucose values from a GTT belong under blood_glucose, not here (DECISIONS.md D-019 step 1).

insulin_sensitivity.label: Insulin sensitivity / insulin tolerance
insulin_sensitivity.notes: As above the reported quantity may be sensitivity or resistance. Also note extreme insulin sensitivity is not simply 'good'. POLARITY: raw glucose values from an ITT belong under blood_glucose, not here (DECISIONS.md D-019 step 1). Only an interpreted sensitivity or resistance result is recorded against this id.

corticosterone.label: Plasma corticosterone / HPA axis output
corticosterone.notes: Includes ACTH as an HPA-axis readout; separate them at extraction if the paper reports both.

gh_secretion.label: Growth hormone secretion
gh_secretion.notes: Lower GH/IGF-1 tone extends lifespan in mice while higher supports growth and lean mass; valence is genuinely contested.

gonadotropins.label: LH/FSH and reproductive hormones
gonadotropins.notes: Deliberately broad; split LH pulse frequency, LH surge, prolactin and gonadal steroids at extraction time if the project later needs them separately. Bare 'LH' must never be matched without context because it collides with lateral hypothalamus.

food_intake.label: Food intake
food_intake.notes: Canonical example of a context-dependent variable: hyperphagia is pathological on a high-fat diet and protective in cachexia.

energy_expenditure.label: Energy expenditure
energy_expenditure.notes: Must be reported with its body-mass normalisation; the normalisation choice changes the sign of many published effects.

rer.label: Respiratory exchange ratio
rer.notes: `fat oxidation` and `lipid oxidation` are inverted: RER is VCO2/VO2, so burning more fat LOWERS it. A single sentence in doi:10.1038/s41467-018-08239-x reports "an increase in RER" and "a decrease in fat utilization" as one finding; following the synonym list without this annotation yields `rer: decrease` from a sentence that supports `rer: increase` (D-049). `substrate utilization` and `fuel preference` name no direction at all and are neither plain nor inverted.

core_temperature.label: Core body temperature
core_temperature.notes: Torpor/hypothermia is protective in some contexts and lethal in others.

bone_density.label: Bone mineral density / bone mass
bone_density.notes: Generally higher BMD is favourable, but osteopetrotic/sclerotic increases are not, and the measurement compartment matters; left null rather than asserting a valence.

il6.label: Circulating IL-6
il6.notes: IL-6 is both a pro-inflammatory cytokine and an exercise-induced myokine with metabolic benefit; no global valence.

inflammatory_markers_other.label: Other inflammatory markers
inflammatory_markers_other.notes: Catch-all bucket. Records landing here should keep outcome_raw verbatim because the bucket is heterogeneous. Includes central glial markers because the hypothalamic-inflammation literature reports them as the systemic-inflammation readout.

sleep.label: Total or composite sleep-wake amount
sleep.notes: The id for a readout that does NOT resolve to one vigilance state: a total, a composite ('sleep-wake amounts'), or a sentence reporting two states jointly ('NREM and REM sleep increased'). Where the paper names one state, the specific id wins -- `nrem_sleep`, `rem_sleep`, `wakefulness`, `sleep_latency`, `sleep_fragmentation` (D-019 step 1, D-064). Until 0.5.0 this was the ONLY sleep id, and NREM, REM, wakefulness, latency, fragmentation and EEG delta power were all synonyms of it, so a paper's NREM time and its wakefulness time landed in one claim cell although they are different quantities that can move independently (D-064). `cataplexy` and `narcolepsy` stay here: they name a state of the whole sleep-wake system rather than an amount of one stage. `EEG delta power` was removed at 0.4.0 as out of scope entirely (D-063): cortical activity is not a state of the organism. `cataplexy` and `narcolepsy` are signed: they name a clinical state, so a paper reporting that mice `developed cataplexy` states the appearance of the state and NOT a change in sleep amount. Under D-021 that is no record at all, not a record with a caveat -- see D-087, where a batch-2 reader proposed `sleep INCREASE` on exactly that sentence.

osmolality_avp.label: Plasma osmolality / vasopressin
osmolality_avp.notes: This id bundles plasma osmolality with AVP, which can move in the opposite direction from it (AVP rises in SIADH while osmolality falls), so a record here should say in `extraction_notes` which of the two its quote measures (D-049). `hyponatremia` and `hypernatremia` are `signed_synonyms`: they name a state and carry their own direction.

estrous_cyclicity.label: Estrous cyclicity
estrous_cyclicity.notes: Includes pubertal timing and reproductive senescence markers because the kisspeptin literature reports them as the same readout family.

median_lifespan.label: Median lifespan
median_lifespan.notes: One of the few cases where a direction is defensible: longer median survival under otherwise equal conditions is the field's accepted benefit. Even so this must not be combined with Tier A outcomes into a score.

frailty_index.label: Frailty index
frailty_index.notes: Defensible because the index is constructed so that accumulated deficits raise the score.

grip_strength.label: Grip strength
grip_strength.notes: Rotarod and hanging-wire are included as functional-strength proxies; they are not the same assay and should be kept apart in outcome_raw.

cognitive_performance.label: Cognitive performance
cognitive_performance.notes: Renamed from `cognitive_decline` at schema v0.2.0 (docs/DECISIONS.md D-029). The old id named both a performance and a decline, so `direction` was ambiguous on its face. `direction` now describes the change in cognitive PERFORMANCE: increase = better. The assay number often runs the other way (escape latency, time to criterion), so per D-019 prefer the literally measured quantity where the vocabulary has one, and otherwise invert the direction to match performance and say so in extraction_notes. higher_is stays null: the measures are not comparable across assays, and this is a Tier B outcome, which SCHEMA.md 6 forbids as a training target.

senescence_markers.label: Cellular senescence markers
senescence_markers.notes: Higher senescent burden is usually described as deleterious, but these markers are also induced by transient stress and by beneficial remodelling (e.g. wound healing), and the panels are not interchangeable. Left null deliberately.

nrem_sleep.label: NREM sleep amount
nrem_sleep.notes: Amount of NREM sleep. Not a complement of `rem_sleep`: a manipulation can raise one and lower the other, which is why pooling them in a single `sleep` id manufactured contradictions (D-064). Slow-wave sleep is included as the same stage under its other name; slow-wave ACTIVITY is delta power and is out of scope (D-063). `NREM` and `non-REM` are listed bare, which is what makes the matcher see the state in "NREM and REM sleep decreased" -- the commonest composite phrasing in this literature, where neither `NREM sleep` nor `non-REM sleep` occurs contiguously and the elided half was silently lost (D-070). Bare `REM` is listed on `rem_sleep` for the mirror reason, with its `non-REM` overlap measured and accepted; see that entry.

rem_sleep.label: REM sleep amount
rem_sleep.notes: Amount of REM sleep. See `nrem_sleep`: the two are separate quantities and are deliberately separate ids (D-064). `REM` is listed bare so the matcher sees the state in "REM and NREM sleep", where `REM sleep` is not contiguous -- 12 of 946 proposed sleep units, the mirror of the 47 in the other ordering (D-070). It is a word-boundary match, so it also fires inside `non-REM sleep`. That was measured before being accepted: of the 25 units mentioning non-REM, all 25 also discuss REM in its own right, so the spurious match never fires alone on this corpus. The trade is deliberate and follows from what this matcher is for -- it proposes candidates a curator accepts or rejects, so a false candidate is reviewable while a missed one is invisible. The precision cost is bounded and visible; the recall cost was neither.

wakefulness.label: Wakefulness amount
wakefulness.notes: Amount of time awake. A quantity in its own right since 0.5.0; it was an `inverted_synonym` of `sleep` before that, which required every curator to flip a direction by hand and left the flip visible only in extraction_notes (D-049, D-064). `direction` here describes the change in WAKEFULNESS: more wake is `increase`. Bare `arousal` is deliberately NOT a synonym of this id or of `sleep_fragmentation`: it names the waking state in one literature and a count of awakenings in the other, and the vocabulary annotates traps rather than resolving them (D-021). A paper saying `arousal` must be read.

sleep_latency.label: Sleep onset latency
sleep_latency.notes: Time to fall asleep, or to a named stage. A quantity in its own right since 0.5.0; it was an `inverted_synonym` of `sleep` before that (longer latency is less sleep). `direction` here describes the change in LATENCY: a longer latency is `increase`.

sleep_fragmentation.label: Sleep fragmentation / continuity
sleep_fragmentation.notes: How broken up sleep is, however the paper quantifies it -- bout count, bout duration, arousal index, transitions. A quantity in its own right since 0.5.0; `sleep fragmentation` was a `signed_synonym` of `sleep` before that. `direction` describes the change in FRAGMENTATION: more broken sleep is `increase`, so a longer mean bout duration is `decrease` and extraction_notes must say which statistic was reported, because bout count and bout duration move in opposite directions for the same underlying change. Bare `arousal` is excluded: see `wakefulness`.
